newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia defiant over challenges to car policy.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia defiant over challenges to car policy.

text.p: Indonesia remained defiant on Friday in the wake of threats by Japan, the European Union and the United States to take its controversial national car policy to the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
"Indonesia will not change its car policy," Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
"We have a policy and we will implement it and we will not change it on principle," Ariwibowo said.

Japan said on Wednesday it would launch a formal complaint to the Geneva-based WTO over the car policy. The European Union (EU) said on Thursday it had decided to follow suit, while the United States has also said it would take the matter to the trde body.
All three say the national car plan, announced earlier this year, violates international trade rules.

The national car policy gives 100 percent tariff and luxury tax exemptions for three years to PT Timor Putra Nasional, a company controlled by Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra, if the firm can meet local content requirements.
This week, PT Timor Putra Nasional began selling its fully imported Timor sedans, made by joint venture partner Kia Motors of South Korea.
It plans to begin assembly of the vehicles next March before commencing full manufacturing in 1998.
The Timor currently is being made in South Korea and imported, but is eventually to be manufactured in Indonesia.
Ariwibowo played down the dispute, saying differences between WTO members were "normal". The EU had already said it wanted to consulte Indonesia over the policy, the minister said.
"We are preparing to have consultations with the EU," he said.
Ariwibowo said he was not worried about retaliatory action.
"It could not be (possible) as we are members of the WTO and there are procedures for members of the WTO," he said.
PT Timor has said it plans to build 200,000 units a year by 1998-99 and to have made one million cars before 2003.
PT Timor Putra Nasional must reach a local component level of 20 percent by the first year of production, 40 percent by the second and 60 percent by the third.
